I would like you to implement a module named TopModule with the following
interface. All input and output ports are one bit unless otherwise
specified.

 - input  a
 - input  b
 - input  c
 - output out

The module should implement the circuit described by the Karnaugh map
below.

          a
   bc   0   1
   00 | 0 | 1 |
   01 | 1 | 1 |
   11 | 1 | 1 |
   10 | 1 | 1 |

This is one fresh independent VerilogEval v2 spec-to-RTL experiment using GPT-6.1 Sol. Work ONLY in this task directory. Read only problem.txt, policy.txt and the supplied experiment helpers. DO NOT use Skills: do not discover, read, invoke, or apply any SKILL.md or skill resources. Both experiment conditions prohibit all Skills. Do not browse, search outside this directory, spawn agents, access official testbenches/reference RTL/evaluation logs, read other problems, or read any previous experiment. Use exactly one Agent. Official evaluation occurs after your turn; no official feedback or retries are available.
HARNESS: the required DUT top module is TopModule (case-sensitive), including when the original text does not specify a top name. Preserve original ports, widths, reset and cycle semantics. These requirements override generic FPGA naming, reset, handshakes conventions. No extra ports or latency. For enum next-state assignment use explicit if/else instead of a ternary to avoid the installed simulator's cast compatibility issue. Do not infer new behavior from generic FPGA practices. No synthesis or board work.
BEFORE implementing the problem run python3 smoke_environment.py. It must report status passed: correct sequential fixture passes, deliberately wrong fixture fails, repaired fixture passes. This checks the actual development environment and is unrelated to the benchmark problem. Do not edit dev_check.py or smoke_environment.py or their evidence.
Create candidate.sv and preserve candidate_initial.sv immediately after initial RTL creation BEFORE any development checks or RTL edits. Create an independent self-checking dev_tb.sv with top dev_tb. Base its oracle on the ORIGINAL problem, including sampling phases, reset, initial unknowns when specified, and directed/boundary cases. For waveform problems replay the original timestamp/edge relationships; do not silently alter the stimulus timing to fit the implementation. Include $fatal on mismatches, a bounded timeout, and an explicit line beginning PASS only after successful checks.
MANDATORY CHECKS: run python3 dev_check.py --label initial, which freezes source/testbench snapshots and runs Icarus 12 with -g2012 -Wall -Wno-timescale and matching vvp. It emits real compile/simulation logs and dev_checks.jsonl. This helper is the primary development evaluator. A PASS means development verification only, not official correctness. The helper also emits supplemental Icarus 11 diagnostics on a v12 compiler crash; these are diagnostic only, not a replacement evaluation.
DEBUG LOOP: if a development check fails, inspect the logs, investigate RTL and testbench against the ORIGINAL specification, and make a justified correction. Do not classify a compiler crash as a reason to immediately submit unchanged RTL: inspect the supplemental diagnostics and source. You may make at most THREE RTL revisions after the initial candidate. Preserve each revision in candidate_revision_1.sv etc. and rerun the fixed helper after each revision, --label revision_1 etc. If the testbench is proven wrong, preserve its old version and explain the correction; never weaken expected values or remove checks just to obtain PASS. Correcting only the TB does not consume an RTL revision. Recheck after TB edits too. Stop at development PASS or after three RTL revisions, keeping all failed evidence. If an infrastructure problem remains, document it explicitly as unverified; do not invent PASS. Complete within a 600-second external deadline.
End with candidate.sv, the unchanged initial snapshot, dev_tb.sv, development evidence, and worker_report.json containing revision_count, checks, development_outcome, limitations, and justified RTL/TB changes. Actual time/tokens/hashes are measured externally; do not invent them. Do not manually edit helper reports or snapshots. Finish concisely.

CONDITION: ordinary single-Agent generation. Solve the original problem directly. Do NOT create explicit contract.json or contract gate and do not use any Skills.
